labelsAvailable.note: Valid absorbed-dose labels exist in the sample sheet. Phase 9 described the dose label as unusable; the label was fine, the evaluation protocol was not matched to the design.

confoundAudit.design: 3 absorbed doses x 4 timepoints x 3 replicates, full factorial
confoundAudit.statement: Dose is not confounded with timepoint: the design is full factorial, so every timepoint contains all three doses. Each (dose, timepoint) cell is a single contiguous sequencing block, so a batch effect cannot be separated from a cell effect; that limits what a cell-level split can mean, and it is why the primary protocol holds out whole timepoints. The Phase 9 note that dose was 'confounded with processing order' is therefore partly right and partly wrong, and the wrong part is the reason a valid dose label was treated as unusable.

A_cellHeldOut.whyItCannotAnswerTheQuestion: Holding out one cell removes an entire (dose, timepoint) combination from training, so 8 of 12 cells share a dose level with the held-out cell but none shares its timepoint. The fold is really asking whether the model can predict an unseen timepoint, and the 3-class accuracy mixes that failure with the dose question.

permutation.scheme: dose labels permuted within timepoint (design-preserving null)

C_timepointHeldOutOrdinal.scheme: leave-one-timepoint-out, ordinal (Ridge on Gy, Spearman rho)

binaryReference.note: The pair bootstrap resamples individual libraries and ignores that three libraries share a cell, so it is narrower than the truth; the group bootstrap resamples the 12 cells. Both are reported because the Phase 9 cross-study reference used the pair version, and the comparison shows how much of its width came from treating correlated replicates as independent.

permutation.scheme: dose labels permuted within timepoint (design-preserving null)

protocolDependence.statement: The same binary contrast scores 0.562 when whole (dose, timepoint) cells are held out and 0.812 when whole timepoints are. The target study does carry a learnable irradiated-vs-control signal, but it lives in variation that does not survive an unseen (dose, timepoint) cell, which is the condition a cross-study transfer actually faces. The cross-study reference therefore stands, with its scope now stated: it measures transfer-analogous generalization, not the absence of signal.

decisionRule: Recover a dose model only if the ordinal Spearman rho is positive, its design-preserving permutation p is below 0.05, and the 3-class accuracy also beats its design-preserving null. Fixed before the run.
disclosure: This does not create a servable model and does not overturn the Phase 9 exclusion. It replaces an unexplained chance-level number with a measured statement about which part of dose is recoverable, on 36 libraries from one genotype and one laboratory, where each (dose, timepoint) cell is a single sequencing batch.
